additions.text: The simple tenses of the indicative mood: facts, routines, the past, the future and hypotheses.
Formed with haber plus the past participle, which never changes.
Wishes, doubts, emotions and clauses that depend on another verb: «quiero que…», «ojalá…», «cuando…».
irregular preterite or future stem (like tener, hacer, poder)
regular, with an irregular past participle
irregular, with forms of its own
gu → gü before e, so the u is still pronounced
c → qu before e, to keep the /k/ sound
g → gu before e, to keep the hard g
z → c before e (Spanish rarely writes ze)
gu → g before a and o, where the u is no longer needed
c → z before a and o, to keep the soft c
g → j before a and o, to keep the /x/ sound
a y is added between the stem and endings that do not start with i
an unstressed i between two vowels is written y, and a stressed i takes an accent
the i of -ió and -iendo disappears after ñ, ll or ch
${cap(verb)} is conjugated like ${base} and keeps all its irregular forms (${join([t.presente[0], t.indefinido[0], t.futuro[0], cj.participle])}).

It has forms of its own that follow no pattern, so learners memorise them, above all the present (${join([t.presente[0], t.presente[1], t.presente[2]])}), the preterite (${join([t.indefinido[0], t.indefinido[2]])}) and the present subjunctive (${t.subjPresente[0]}).
Ser and ir share the same preterite (fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fuisteis, fueron) and imperfect subjunctive (fuera). Context tells them apart: «fue profesora» (ser) versus «fue al mercado» (ir).
As an auxiliary it forms every compound tense (he hablado, había comido). Meaning «there is / there are» it is impersonal and stays in the third person singular: hay, hubo, había, habrá, haya.
It is irregular in the present (estoy, está), the preterite (estuve, estuvo) and the present subjunctive (esté). With a gerund it forms the progressive: «está trabajando».
«Ir a + infinitive» expresses plans and intentions: «voy a estudiar». The nosotros command is «vamos».
It is defective: it is used mainly in the present and imperfect followed by an infinitive («suele llegar tarde», «solía leer mucho»). The future and the imperative are not used.
It is a weather verb: in normal use it only appears in the third person singular (${join([t.presente[2], t.indefinido[2], t.imperfecto[2], t.futuro[2]])}).

Stem change ${change} whenever the stress falls on the stem: ${join([spec.yo ? "" : t.presente[0], t.presente[1], t.presente[2], t.presente[5]])}. Nosotros and vosotros keep the original vowel: ${join([t.presente[3], t.presente[4]])}.${spec.yo ? "" : ` The same change appears in the present subjunctive (${t.subjPresente[0]}) and the tú command (${t.imperativo[1]}).`}
The same change appears in the present subjunctive (${t.subjPresente[0]}) and the tú command (${t.imperativo[1]}).

As an -ir verb it also changes ${spec.stem === "ie" ? "e → i" : "o → u"} in the third person preterite (${join([t.indefinido[2], t.indefinido[5]])}), the gerund (${cj.gerund}), nosotros in the present subjunctive (${t.subjPresente[3]}) and the whole imperfect subjunctive (${t.subjImperfecto[0]}).

Stem change e → i when the stress falls on the stem (${join([t.presente[0], t.presente[1], t.presente[2], t.presente[5]])}), in the third person preterite (${join([t.indefinido[2], t.indefinido[5]])}), the gerund (${cj.gerund}) and the whole present and imperfect subjunctive (${join([t.subjPresente[0], t.subjImperfecto[0]])}).

The ${spec.stem} takes a written accent when stressed, which keeps it apart from the next vowel: ${join([t.presente[0], t.presente[1], t.presente[2], t.presente[5]])}. Nosotros has no accent (${t.presente[3]}). The accent comes back in the present subjunctive (${t.subjPresente[0]}).

Only the first person present is irregular: ${t.presente[0]} (c → zc). Because the present subjunctive is built on that form, all of it carries zc: ${join(t.subjPresente.slice(0, 3))}… Everything else is regular.
The first person present is irregular: ${t.presente[0]}. The present subjunctive is built on it: ${join(t.subjPresente.slice(0, 3))}…

Irregular preterite stem in j: ${join([t.indefinido[0], t.indefinido[2], t.indefinido[5]])}. After j the ellos form ends in -eron, not -ieron. The imperfect subjunctive inherits the stem: ${t.subjImperfecto[0]}.

Strong preterite with an irregular stem: ${join([t.indefinido[0], t.indefinido[2], t.indefinido[5]])}. The yo and él forms end in unstressed -e and -o, with no accent. The imperfect subjunctive inherits the stem: ${t.subjImperfecto[0]}.
Irregular future and conditional stem: ${join([t.futuro[0], t.futuro[2], t.condicional[0]])}. The endings are regular.
Irregular past participle: ${cj.participle}. It forms every compound tense («${t.perfecto[2]}») and also works as an adjective.
Spelling change: ${SPELLING_EN[sp.key]} (${join(examples)}). The pronunciation stays regular.
${cap(verb)} is a regular -${e} verb, conjugated like ${MODEL_REGULAR[e]}: the stem ${verb.slice(0, -2)}- plus the endings of each tense.
